title: CIA Triad, Threat Modeling & Attack Surface
summary: Establish security engineering judgment built on Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Least Privilege, and STRIDE threat modeling.
learningObjectives: Classify real-world incidents by Confidentiality, Integrity, or Availability impact
Decompose application trust boundaries cleanly using the STRIDE methodology

sections.heading: 1. The CIA Triad & Defense in Depth
sections.content:
Every cybersecurity control defends one or more pillars of the CIA Triad: Confidentiality (preventing unauthorized reads via encryption & RBAC), Integrity (preventing tampering via cryptographic signatures & HMAC), and Availability (preserving resilient service under failures or DDoS via redundancy & rate limits).

Rather than gambling everything on one perimeter firewall, engineers stack Defense in Depth—pairing network firewalls, TLS, MFA, parameterized queries, strict access checks, and audit logs so breaching one control still stops the attacker.

codeExamples.code:
[Internet Client] -> [WAF / Rate Limiter] -> [TLS Edge Termination]
                         | Security Header Checks & IP Throttling
                         v
[Verified Session Auth] -> [Object Ownership Authorization] -> [Parameterized DB Query]
                                                                  (Encrypted at Rest + Audit Log)
codeExamples.explanation: Defense in depth ensures multiple independent validation gates inspect requests from edge to storage.

keyPoints: Confidentiality != Integrity: encrypted ciphertexts without MAC/AEAD tags can still be flipped/tampered.
Least Privilege restricts identities strictly to required capabilities.
commonMistakes: Security through obscurity (relying on undocumented URLs or hidden JS UI buttons rather than server authorization).

sections.heading: 2. STRIDE Threat Modeling Before Deployment
sections.content: Before launching APIs, defenders trace data flows across trust boundaries and systematically inspect all six STRIDE risks: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege.

codeExamples.code:
### STRIDE Pre-Launch Security Checklist: Password Reset Endpoint
- **Spoofing**: Require high-entropy single-use cryptographic token hashed in DB, NEVER predictable incremental IDs.
- **Tampering**: Deliver reset token strictly via verified TLS HTTPS; bind token to exact userId.
- **Repudiation**: Log immutable timestamped reset requests and completions cleanly.
- **Info Disclosure**: Always display generic response ("If account exists, email sent") avoiding user email enumeration.
- **DoS**: Apply per-IP & per-account sliding window rate limits.
codeExamples.explanation: Generic HTTP responses combined with high-entropy one-time hashed tokens eliminate classic password-reset leaks.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Verified threat mitigation plan neutralizing token prediction, account enumeration, and abuse

keyPoints: Never confirm whether an arbitrary email exists during public login/reset flows unless intentionally required.
commonMistakes: Returning `'Email does not exist'` vs `'Wrong password'`, giving attackers free automated account lists.

exercises.title: STRIDE Assessment on Student File Upload API
exercises.objective: Identify spoofing, disclosure, and DoS risks on a naive `/api/upload` endpoint.
exercises.description: A student team releases `/api/upload` accepting files up to 500MB with no login check and writing raw filenames directly onto disk `/public/files/<originalName>`.
instructions: Identify the Spoofing and DoS risks of unbounded unauthenticated 500MB uploads.
Explain the Path Traversal / RCE hazard of trusting `originalName` (e.g., `../../index.html`).
List 3 concrete hardening steps solving these threats.
exercises.starterCode:
# Threat Review: /api/upload
- Unauthenticated 500MB DoS Fix: ...
- Raw originalName Traversal Fix: ...
- Serving Safety Fix: ...
hints: Enforce auth, strict max byte limits (e.g., 5MB), magic-byte inspection, and random UUID filenames.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Authenticating uploaders, capping sizes, renaming files with UUIDs, checking MIME magic bytes, and isolating file serving shut down path traversal and XSS.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Which security pillar protects bank ledger amounts from being altered during transit or storage?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Integrity ensures trustworthiness and protects data against unauthorized tampering.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why does returning 'No account found for alice@corp.com' enable attackers during password resets?

options.text: It enables silent User Enumeration allowing attackers to harvest registered user emails

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Consistent generic reset messages prevent leaking account existence.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: In STRIDE threat modeling, 'E' stands for which risk (such as tampering a JWT claim to gain admin role)?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Elevation of Privilege covers unauthorized capability escalation.

recap: You applied CIA Triad reasoning, Defense in Depth controls, and structured STRIDE threat modeling cleanly.
